etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English lovere, luffer, lufere, equivalent to love +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: One who loves and cares for another person in a romantic way; a sweetheart, love, soulmate, boyfriend, girlfriend, or spouse.

quote.citation: c. 1596–1598 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Merchant of Venice”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene vi], page 170, column 2:
quote.text: […] loue is blinde, and louers cannot ſee / The pretty follies that themſelues commit, […]

quote.citation: 1976, Joni Mitchell (lyrics and music), “Song For Sharon”, in Hejira:
quote.text: Well there's a wide wide world of noble causes / And lovely landscapes to discover / But all I really want to do right now / Is find another lover

quote.citation: 2014 September 23, Elle King, Dave Bassett, “Ex's & Oh's”, in Love Stuff‎[1], performed by Elle King:
quote.text: Now, there's one in California who's been cursing my name / 'Cause I found me a better lover in the UK, hey, hey / Until I made my getaway

quote.citation: 2016, David Boulter, Stuart A. Staples (lyrics and music), “Like Only Lovers Can”, in The Waiting Room, performed by Tindersticks:
quote.text: We can only hurt each other the way that lovers can / So where do we go, where do we hide now?

definitions.definition: A sexual partner, especially one with whom someone is having an affair.

quote.citation: 2006, Peifer Yann, Reuter Manuel (lyrics and music), “Bad Boy”, in Everytime We Touch, performed by Cascada, →OCLC:
quote.text: Be my bad boy, be my man / Be my weekend lover, but don't be my friend / You can be my bad boy, but understand / That I don't need you in my life again

quote.citation: 2018 January 17, "Libra Woman: Personality Traits: Love & More", Astrology.com [2]
quote.text: A Libra woman seems to always be in love - either with her long term partner or with an ever-changing series of rotating lovers.

quote.citation: 1888–1891, Herman Melville, “[Billy Budd, Foretopman.] Chapter XVIII.”, in Billy Budd and Other Stories, London: John Lehmann, published 1951, →OCLC, page 279:
quote.text: But though a conscientious disciplinarian he was no lover of authority for mere authority's sake.

definitions.definition: (West Country, with "my") An informal term of address for any friend.
